sights.address: Burrows Park, Lake Mendota shore (north side), Madison, WI
sights.w: A bird effigy with a 128-foot wingspan in a small lakeshore park — one of the best-preserved of Madison's effigy mounds (NRHP). Free.
Two animal effigies — a lynx and a bear — plus a linear mound on the Lake Monona side of the east isthmus (NRHP). Free.

sights.address: Bear Mound Park, Vilas Circle, Madison, WI
sights.w: An intact bear effigy (only a leg section lost) in tiny Bear Mound Park by Vilas Park, NRHP-listed with the nearby Curtis Mounds; Vilas Park itself holds a seven-mound group. Free.

sights.address: Observatory Hill, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI
sights.w: A bird effigy and a rare two-tailed water-spirit mound just west of Washburn Observatory, overlooking Lake Mendota (NRHP). Free.

sights.address: Edgewood campus, Woodrow St off Monroe St, Madison, WI
sights.w: Twelve preserved mounds on the Edgewood campus — a linear mound and six conicals visible from Edgewood Drive (NRHP archaeological district). Free.

sights.address: Weeks Hall, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI
sights.w: Free campus museum in Weeks Hall: Wisconsin's deep past in rocks, fossils, meteorites, a fluorescent-mineral room, dinosaurs and a mastodon skeleton.
